label: COMMUNICATION

cover.headline: Sharing *the mental load* without resentment
cover.sub: 5 ways to ask for real help.

points.heading: Make the invisible visible
points.body: Write down everything you track, not just the tasks you do.
points.panel: List every recurring job, from appointments to birthday gifts.

points.heading: Pick a calm moment
points.body: Not in the middle of a messy kitchen.
points.panel: “Can we sit down this weekend and look at how we split things?”

points.heading: Hand over whole jobs
points.body: Owning a task from start to finish beats helping with pieces.
points.panel: “Could you fully own school forms from now on?”

points.heading: Let it be done differently
points.body: His way may not be yours, and that’s okay.
points.panel: “I’ll leave that one to you completely.”

points.heading: Check in after a month
points.body: Adjust what isn’t working, without blame.
points.panel: “How’s the new split feeling for you?”

close.save: Save this for your next sit-down.

caption:
Resentment often builds around the work nobody sees: remembering, planning, and keeping track of everything.

Sharing it fairly starts with making it visible, then handing over whole jobs, not just tasks. These five steps help you ask for real help without a fight, so you both feel the difference.
